gallery.title: File:MSH82 st helens plume from harrys ridge 05-19-82.jpg
gallery.credit:
CVO Photo Archive Mount St. Helens, Washington

Before, During, and After 18 May 1980.
gallery.source: MSH82 st helens plume from harrys ridge 05-19-82
gallery.description: Plumes of steam, gas, and ash often occurred at Mount St. Helens in the early 1980s. On clear days they could be seen from Portland, Oregon, 50 mi (80 km) to the south. The plume photographed here rose nearly 3,000 ft (910 m) above the volcano's rim. The view is from Harrys Ridge, 5 mi (8 km) north of the mountain.

gallery.title: File:Hanging around (7913845348).jpg
gallery.artist: John Fowler from Placitas, NM, USA
gallery.description: Some sea kayakers were camping by my cabin at the Hobuck Beach Resort, near Neah Bay, Washington. I wish I had gotten some shots of them paddling out on the ocean. All I got was these dry suits hanging on a tree branch. Sea kayaking would seem to be an ideal way to get to the hard to reach places along the coast. I suspect, though, that the enthusiasm would wear off fast for somebody like me without much upper body strength.
